summary: The portfolio page timeouts are caused by config change cfg-2207, an automated infra-automation "small" cost-optimisation profile that cut portfolio-service's HikariCP datasource pool from 50 to 5 at 09:52:13Z and was never reverted. The pool immediately pinned at exactly the 5-connection ceiling with zero variance (F16/F25), application threads queued (HikariPool total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=25–57; F18/F27), each request waited ~3s on a JDBC acquire and held its upstream connection open, so portfolio-service p99 stepped to ~4.25s with an ~22% error rate (F15/F28) and the gateway — with flat CPU/memory and a held-open-until-timeout 504 signature — followed 34s later at 09:53:53Z (F9/F11/F17). Load and CPU were flat through onset (F29), which rules out a traffic surge, and the gateway HTTP/2 upgrade (08:00Z) is contradicted: the pool sat stable at ~11.6–12.3 connections for ~113 minutes after that deploy and the onset tracks the 09:52 config change, not the deploy (F26/F13/F14). Confidence 0.78 (high, capped by the Critic at 0.85); the gateway is a victim, not the cause.

ranked_hypotheses.title: portfolio-service DB connection-pool shrink (cfg-2207) starves /v1/portfolio/holdings; gateway 504s are a symptom
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 09:52:13Z an automated infra-automation job applied the 'small' cost-optimisation profile to portfolio-service, cutting its HikariCP datasource pool from 50 to 5 (cfg-2207, never reverted, F2/F22). The pool cap became effective in the 09:53 bucket: db_pool_in_use drops from ~11.5-12.5 to a hard pinned 5.0 with zero variance (F16/F25) while request_rate (~550-580 rps) and cpu (~35%) are unchanged (F29), so the pin is caused by the size limit, not by load or CPU. Application threads then queue for a connection: the first ERROR at 09:53:19Z is 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings (F17), escalating to explicit HikariPool exhaustion 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' with 25-57 waiters (F18/F27). Each request now waits ~3s and holds its upstream connection open, so portfolio-service p99 steps from ~173ms to ~4.25s in the 09:53 minute (F15), portfolio-service error_rate jumps ~90x to ~22% (F28), and the gateway — whose own CPU/memory stay flat (F11) — holds connections to timeout and emits the identical 'upstream timeout to portfolio-service' 504 WARN, first at 09:53:53Z, 34s after the upstream acquire failure (F9/F17) and one minute after the gateway's own 5xx onset (F14). The gateway is a victim.

causal_chain.claim: infra-automation applies cost-optimisation 'small' profile to portfolio-service, db.pool.max_size 50->5 at 09:52Z; applied in-log at 09:52:13Z; never reverted
Pool cap takes effect: db_pool_in_use falls from ~11.5-12.5 to a pinned 5.0 from the 09:53 bucket onward, with zero headroom
The pin is not load- or CPU-driven: request_rate holds ~550-580 rps and cpu ~35-38% straight through onset
Threads cannot acquire a connection; HikariCP 3s acquire timeouts and pool exhaustion with waiting=25-57, active=5, idle=0
portfolio-service p99 steps from ~173ms to ~4.25s in the same 09:53 minute and error_rate jumps ~90x to ~22%

Requests are held open past the gateway's upstream timeout; gateway emits route-specific 'upstream timeout to portfolio-service' 504 WARNs (held-open, not fast-fail), first gateway 504 at 09:53:53Z 34s after the upstream acquire error
Gateway p99 saturates ~4.2-4.6s from the 09:53 bucket and 5xx steps to ~7% at 09:54, while gateway CPU (~42%) and memory (~58%) remain flat

assumptions: The HikariCP 'total=5' in the log is the same ceiling as the reduced max_size (the pool gauge itself is not exposed; F30).
portfolio-service's /holdings handler acquires a DB connection per request and holds it for the request duration (not directly instrumented beyond the observed waiter/waiting counts).

No concurrent shared-datastore fault is also in play: ledger-db/redis-cache metrics were not sampled (gap). A concurrent store slowdown would not by itself produce a pool pinned at exactly the 5-connection ceiling.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared datastore (ledger-db or redis-cache) slow, degrading portfolio-service via a neighbour
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db and redis-cache are shared:true and on the /v1/portfolio/* path (F4/F5/F19/F20). A shared-store fault (failover, lock contention, neighbour load) could slow portfolio-service's DB/cache calls and present as gateway 504s. Precedent HIST-102. This remains untested — no ledger-db/redis-cache latency/error/connection metrics were sampled — but the measured failure mode here is pool-acquire starvation against a shrunk pool (active=5, idle=0, waiting=43-57, total=5) rather than slow queries, which is not what a slow store produces; and there were no deployments on either store in the window (F23).

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db / redis-cache are shared stores on the portfolio path, reachable by neighbours
A shared-store fault (failover/lock contention/neighbour load) would slow ledger-db or redis-cache
portfolio-service DB/cache calls block to ~4s, its p99 rises

assumptions: An unmeasured shared-store fault coexists, but would have to explain a pool pinned at exactly the new 5-connection ceiling while the pre-change pool sat at ~12 with headroom.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Gateway HTTP/2 envoy 1.30 upgrade (v9.3.0) mishandles upstreams to portfolio-service
ranked_hypotheses.statement: api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00Z upgraded the envoy filter chain (1.29->1.30) and enabled HTTP/2 to upstreams (F1). The new HTTP/2 upstream path could reset/hang portfolio-service responses, producing hold-open 504s on /v1/portfolio/*. This is the reporter's suspicion and matches HIST-116. However no telemetry ties the deploy to onset: the gateway p99 step is a single clean bucket at 09:53Z (F13) with flat gateway CPU/memory (F11), and the co-degradation is on the upstream side, where Hikari acquire errors start 34s before the first gateway 504 (F17).

causal_chain.claim: api-gateway v9.3.0 deploys at 08:00Z enabling HTTP/2 to upstreams (envoy 1.29->1.30)
New HTTP/2 upstream handling would need to hang only the portfolio route while other routes stay healthy
Requests held open until upstream timeout -> 504 on /v1/portfolio/*

assumptions: A latent HTTP/2 defect stayed silent for ~113 minutes after deploy and then tripped under unchanged load (request_rate flat, F29).
The envoy deploy at 08:00 would have to hang portfolio calls while the upstream's own measured failure mode is a DB-pool acquire timeout, which no HTTP/2 defect would produce.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity/load surge saturates portfolio-service's pool with no faulty change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge in portfolio-page traffic (or a long-held-query pattern) exhausted portfolio-service capacity independent of any change. Directly contradicted by measurement: request_rate is flat at ~550-580 rps across 09:20-10:14Z (mean 565.0) and cpu stays ~34-38% through onset (F29), and the pre-onset pool sat comfortably at ~11.6-12.3 connections with headroom above 5 (F26). Load did not rise; the ceiling dropped.

causal_chain.claim: Traffic/load on /v1/portfolio/* rises and saturates portfolio-service
Requests queue and time out at the gateway

assumptions: A hidden load surge exists despite the flat, measured request_rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F29 shows request_rate flat at ~550-580 rps and CPU ~35% straight through onset, and F26 shows the pre-onset pool at ~11.6-12.3 with headroom, so no capacity/load surge occurred. The pool pinned at exactly the newly-lowered 5-connection ceiling (F16/F25), a limit set by cfg-2207 (F2), not by demand.

facts.statement: At 09:52:13Z portfolio-service logged 'config change cfg-2207 applied: db.pool.max_size=5', an infra-automation 'small' cost-optimisation profile that cut the datasource pool from 50 to 5; it is the only config change on the portfolio path and its author is infra-automation.
cfg-2207 was never reverted: it is still the latest/only portfolio-service config change through 2026-03-10T12:00Z and there is no revert entry in the 08:00–11:59Z all-services window.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was steady at ~11.5–12.5 connections until 09:50Z (6-min buckets 07:45–09:51Z all ~11.6–12.3, max 13.3), then dropped to 8.45 in the 09:52 bucket and pinned at exactly 5.0 with zero variance from 09:53Z onward — confirming the max_size reduction became effective in the 09:53 bucket.
The pool pin is a size limit, not demand: request_rate held ~550–580 rps (mean 565.0) across 09:20–10:14Z and cpu_pct stayed ~34–38% (mean 35.88) straight through onset.

The first portfolio-service error is at 09:53:19Z, an ERROR 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' — preceding the first gateway 504 at 09:53:53Z by 34 seconds; no ERROR-level logs exist before 09:53:19Z.

Pool-exhaustion is explicit in portfolio-service logs from 09:54:29Z: 'HikariPool-1 - Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)', with waiting queues of 25–57 threads against total=5, active=5, idle=0.

portfolio-service p99 shows a clean single-bucket step at 09:53:00Z at 1-min resolution (09:51=177.51ms, 09:52=172.69ms, then 09:53=4250.91ms, 09:54=4546.3ms), and portfolio-service error_rate jumps ~90x from ~0.14–0.28% to ~22% in the 09:54 bucket, holding ~21.6–23.2%.

api-gateway p99 rises as a genuine step change beginning in the 09:53:00Z bucket at 1-min resolution (09:51 avg=201.64ms, 09:52 avg=200.33ms, 09:53 avg=4418.76ms), with the 5xx error rate stepping up one minute later at 09:54:00Z (~7.18%).

Every one of the 252 recurring gateway WARN entries has the same signature — 'upstream timeout to portfolio-service' on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings returning 504 — i.e. connections held open until timeout rather than fast 502/connection-refused failures, first at 09:53:53Z.
api-gateway resource metrics are not saturated: CPU ~38–47% (avg 42.01) and memory ~51–64% (avg 57.94), flat versus the pre-incident baseline.

The only deployment in the entire 2026-03-09T00:00Z–2026-03-10T11:59Z window is api-gateway v9.3.0 at 08:00:00Z ('Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams', envoy 1.29->1.30), live and never rolled back.

No deployments touched ledger-db or redis-cache in 08:00–12:00Z (count 0 each) and there were zero deployments across all services in 09:00–11:59Z, so the shared stores saw no change-induced restart or failover in the window.

The only non-portfolio gateway WARN signals in the window are isolated and pre/post-date onset (TLS cipher warning 07:27:55, connection-reset retry 08:28:11, clock-drift warning 10:38:45), consistent with errors concentrated on the portfolio route.

The /v1/portfolio/* path is api-gateway -> portfolio-service (http) -> ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http), redis-cache (cache); ledger-db and redis-cache are marked shared:true and are reached by four and four neighbour services respectively.
Beyond the portfolio pool shrink and the earlier gateway upgrade, no other change was active on the portfolio path at 11:59Z.

portfolio-service does not expose a pool-size gauge, connection-acquire wait time, in-flight or queue-depth metric; its available_metrics are cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts, so the 5-connection ceiling and waiter counts were read from the HikariPool error logs.
Queries for portfolio-service metrics request_error_rate and db_pool_size failed with not_found, confirming the pool-size gauge is not exposed under those names.

assumptions: The HikariCP 'total=5' in the log is the same ceiling as the reduced max_size; the pool-size gauge itself is not exposed (F30).
Each /v1/portfolio/holdings request acquires a DB connection and holds it for the request duration; this is not directly instrumented beyond the observed waiter and waiting counts.

No concurrent shared-datastore fault is also in play: ledger-db/redis-cache metrics were never sampled. A concurrent store slowdown would not by itself produce a pool pinned at exactly the 5-connection ceiling with zero variance.
The pre-change HikariPool total=50 was never observed directly in a log line; the 50 value rests on the config-change record (F2/F22) plus the pre-onset db_pool_in_use plateau of ~11.6–12.3 (F26).

timeline.event: Only deployment in the window: api-gateway v9.3.0, 'Upgrade envoy filter chain; enable HTTP/2 to upstreams' (envoy 1.29 -> 1.30), status live, rolled_back_at null.
portfolio-service db_pool_in_use still steady at ~11.5–12.5 connections (6-min buckets 07:45–09:51Z all ~11.6–12.3); baseline gateway p99 ~200ms, portfolio-service p99 ~172–191ms.

Pool pins at exactly 5.0 with zero variance; gateway p99 and portfolio-service p99 both step in this same minute (gateway 09:53 avg=4418.76ms; portfolio-service 09:53=4250.91ms) after flat baseline at 09:51/09:52.
First portfolio-service ERROR: 'GET /v1/portfolio/holdings failed: could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' — the upstream acquire failure preceds the gateway symptom.
First api-gateway WARN: 'upstream timeout to portfolio-service' on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings returning 504 — 34s after the upstream acquire failure, 100s after the config application.

recommended_actions.action: Revert config change cfg-2207 on portfolio-service (restore db.pool.max_size from 5 back to 50) via infra-automation change control, then confirm the new value is applied and effective.
recommended_actions.rationale: cfg-2207 is the only change on the portfolio path at onset, is never reverted (F22/F24), and its 09:52:13Z application is immediately followed by the pool pinning at exactly 5.0 with zero variance (F16/F25) and by HikariCP acquire-timeout errors (F17/F18/F27). Restoring the ceiling removes the resource that is causing requests to queue.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery after the revert: watch portfolio-service db_pool_in_use to confirm headroom returns above 5 (back toward ~11–12), and confirm the HikariCP 'total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=…' acquire-timeout errors and portfolio-service error_rate (~22%) stop.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool being pinned at exactly 5.0 with waiters is the decisive measured mechanism (F16/F18/F27) and error_rate jumped ~90x at the same moment (F28); these are the exact signals that should reverse when the ceiling is restored.

recommended_actions.action: Verify the gateway recovers as a victim: confirm gateway p99 returns from ~4.2–4.6s toward the ~200ms baseline, gateway 5xx falls from ~7% to ~0.2%, and 'upstream timeout to portfolio-service' 504 WARNs stop; do NOT roll back api-gateway v9.3.0 as the primary mitigation.
recommended_actions.rationale: Gateway CPU/memory stayed flat (F11) and every gateway WARN is a held-open upstream timeout that began 34s after the upstream acquire failure (F9/F17), so the gateway is downstream of the fault; the deploy produced no portfolio-path effect for ~113 minutes (F26).

recommended_actions.action: If latency/errors do not recover fully after the revert, immediately sample ledger-db and redis-cache latency, error-rate and connection metrics for the 09:00–10:10Z window to discriminate H3 (shared-store fault) from residual H1 effects.
recommended_actions.rationale: H3 was never directly tested — no ledger-db/redis-cache time-series was collected — and it is the only remaining live alternative to H1; it can be ruled in or out with a single metric query round.

recommended_actions.action: Add a guardrail to the infra-automation cost-optimisation profile: cap how far a 'small' profile may shrink a datasource pool (or require a minimum pool size relative to measured peak connections) and require a canary/step-down before applying pool reductions to production services.
recommended_actions.rationale: A 50->5 (10x) reduction was applied automatically with no observed canary, dropping the pool below the ~11.6–12.3 connections the service actually used (F25/F26) and pinning it at the new ceiling.

recommended_actions.action: Expose the missing portfolio-service signals — db_pool_size (ceiling), connection-acquire wait time, in-flight/queue depth — and alert on pool saturation and acquire-timeout rate, since these had to be reconstructed from HikariPool error logs.
recommended_actions.rationale: portfolio-service exposes no pool-size gauge or acquire-wait metric (F30), so the 5-connection ceiling and waiter counts came only from log samples (F18/F27); an alert on pool-in-use == ceiling with waiters would have caught this at 09:52.

recommended_actions.action: Alert on config changes to connection-pool settings on request-path services and require a pre-change check that the new pool size exceeds observed peak db_pool_in_use.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pool shrank below measured usage (~12) with no automated check comparing the proposed 5 against observed demand, and no alert fired on the config change itself (F2/F22/F25/F26).

recommended_actions.action: Re-run the untaken confirmation queries to close the evidence gaps: sub-bucket gateway timing vs the 08:00Z deploy, per-route/per-upstream gateway metrics (/v1/portfolio/* vs auth/accounts/market-data), and ledger-db/redis-cache health for 09:00–10:10Z.
recommended_actions.rationale: These were left uncollected due to tool-budget exhaustion; they would independently confirm route-specificity, the deploy being non-causal, and the absence of a concurrent shared-store fault underpinning H3.

data_gaps: No ledger-db or redis-cache latency/error/connection metrics were ever sampled for 09:00–10:10Z, so H3 (shared-datastore slowdown) remains directly untested; the conclusion rests on the shape of the failure (acquire-queue starvation against a pool pinned at exactly 5) rather than on direct evidence of store health.

portfolio-service's own metric names request_error_rate and db_pool_size are not exposed (queries failed not_found); the 5-connection ceiling came from HikariCP log fields (total=5) rather than a pool-size gauge, and acquire-wait distribution / queue depth are unmeasured beyond sampled log values.
The pre-change HikariPool total=50 was never observed in a log line; the 50 value rests on the config-change record plus the pre-onset db_pool_in_use plateau of ~11.6–12.3.

Route-specificity is inferred from the log pattern (isolated non-portfolio WARNs) but per-route/per-upstream gateway metrics (/v1/portfolio/* vs auth/accounts/market-data over 09:40–10:10Z) were never queried.

Neighbour-service traffic on the shared ledger-db / redis-cache (order-service, payment-service, auth-service) in 09:00–10:10Z was not measured, so a neighbour-load contribution to a store slowdown cannot be fully excluded.

No cluster/infra events (node scaling, DB failover, lock contention) were available to query; only deployment lists were checked (count 0 for both stores), so an unreported infra event on the shared stores is not fully excluded.
The exact api-gateway v9.3.0 deploy log line was not retrieved, so the deploy-to-onset gap is quantified only from the change record (08:00Z), not from a gateway log marker.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Direct ledger-db or redis-cache metrics showing a latency/error/connection anomaly or a failover/lock-contention event starting ~09:45–09:52Z, which would revive H3 as a contributing or alternative cause.

Evidence that portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was already at or near 5 before 09:52Z, or that the pool ceiling was never actually reduced, which would break the causal link between cfg-2207 and the pin.

HikariPool logs showing waiters or acquire timeouts with a pool ceiling well above 5 (i.e. requests queueing despite headroom), which would indicate a slow store or slow query rather than size-induced starvation.
A verified deploy or change on ledger-db / redis-cache, or a portfolio-service or gateway change, at ~09:52Z other than cfg-2207.
Sub-minute resolution showing gateway/portfolio degradation beginning before 09:52:13Z (e.g. tracking the 08:00Z HTTP/2 upgrade rather than the config change), which would support H2.
Requests in flight before 09:52 continuing to succeed with p99 ~200ms after the config change, which would show the pool shrink had no causal effect.

findings.statement: portfolio-service's only direct dependencies are ledger-db (db), market-data-service (http) and redis-cache (cache) — so any portfolio latency must route through one of these three, and gateway->portfolio-service is the only http edge into it.

cfg-2207 (portfolio-service db.pool.max_size 50 -> 5, changed_at 2026-03-10T09:52:00Z, author infra-automation) is STILL the latest/only portfolio-service config change through 2026-03-10T12:00Z — it was never reverted, and there is no revert entry in the all-services window 08:00-11:59Z.

No deployments at all on ledger-db or redis-cache in 2026-03-10T08:00Z-12:00Z (count:0 each), and zero deployments across all services in 09:00-11:59Z — so no restart/failover was introduced by a deployment on the shared stores in the window.

Because cfg-2207 was never reverted and no deployment/config change touched ledger-db or redis-cache, the only change still active on the portfolio path at 11:59Z is the 50->5 pool shrink, plus the earlier api-gateway v9.3.0 upgrade.

portfolio-service db_pool_in_use was steady at ~11.5-12.5 connections until 09:50Z, then dropped to 8.45 (max 11.89) in the 09:52 bucket, and was pinned at exactly the 5-connection ceiling (avg=max=5.0, zero variance) for every 2-min bucket from 09:54 to 10:14Z. Pool saturation therefore begins at ~09:52, not at 08:00 or at first post-deploy traffic.

The pool was NOT pinned or elevated earlier in the day: 6-min buckets from 07:45 to 09:51Z all show db_pool_in_use between ~11.6 and ~12.3 (max up to 13.3), i.e. comfortably above 5 and stable before 09:52. This kills H2/H4 as an early-onset pool problem and shows the pre-onset pool was not near any ceiling of 5.

portfolio-service emits HikariCP pool-exhaustion errors with explicit waiters: 'Connection is not available, request timed out after 3000ms (total=5, active=5, idle=0, waiting=43)' (47 occurrences) and 'could not acquire JDBC connection within 3000ms' on GET /v1/portfolio/holdings (38 occurrences); ERROR logs start 09:53:19Z, 85 total WARN+ errors returned in 09:20-10:15Z, all ERROR level, none before 09:53:19Z.

findings.statement: portfolio-service error_rate is flat ~0.14-0.28% through 09:52Z, then jumps to 22.3% in the 09:54 bucket and holds ~21.6-23.2% through 10:14Z — a ~90x step change at the same 09:52-09:54 moment the pool pins at 5.

Load into portfolio-service is NOT elevated around onset: request_rate holds ~550-580 req/s across 09:20-10:14Z (mean 565.0, first 568.44, last 552.59), and cpu_pct stays ~34-38% (mean 35.88, max 38.67) straight through the onset — so the pool pin is not explained by a CPU or traffic surge.
findings.verification_note: 2/3 refs verified (tc-022: quote not found in tool output)

findings.statement: portfolio-service does not expose the exact metric names db_pool_size, request_error_rate, connection-acquire wait time, in-flight or queue depth; its available_metrics are cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts. Pool ceiling (5 = total) and waiter counts had to be read from the HikariPool ERROR logs instead.

H1 is confirmed at the decisive measurement: pool saturation and connection-acquire waiters begin at ~09:52-09:54Z — after the 09:52 cfg-2207 pool shrink from 50 to 5 and only ~1-2 min before portfolio-service error_rate and latency step up, exactly matching the config-change time, and NOT at 08:00 (deploy) or earlier. Interpretation: the shrink is the pacing event for the portfolio-service side of the outage.
